subject: Numeracy
title: Rectangles and ovals
objectives: Children will name rectangle and oval.
Children will sort shapes by name.
teachingActivities: Compare a rectangle with a square (two long and two short sides) and an oval with a circle (an egg shape); use real objects such as books, doors, eggs and mirrors; trace shapes with fingers; sort and name all five shapes.
learnerActivities: Name rectangle and oval and sort shapes by name.
resources: Card shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle, oval
assessment: Observe whether each child names rectangle and oval and sorts five shapes by name.

lessons.title: Rectangles
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will name a rectangle and say it has two long and two short sides.
successCriteria: Counts four sides and four corners
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name circle, square and triangle and count and join groups.
lessons.starter: Hold up a book and say "This book is a rectangle. It has two long sides and two short sides."
teacherActivities: Show a rectangle and trace its sides.
Count four sides and four corners.
Compare a rectangle with a square.
learnerActivities: Child points to the long sides.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a rectangle and trace its sides. Children: Children trace the shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Count four sides and four corners. Children: Children count with the teacher.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare a rectangle with a square. Children: Child points to the long sides.
Step 4. Teacher: Find rectangles in the room. Children: Child finds a rectangle.

practical.title: Find rectangles
practical.safety: Use smooth card shapes and supervise the walk. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Compare a rectangle and a square side by side.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a rectangle with straws.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the shapes away and say rectangle.
lessons.homeConnection: Find rectangles at home such as doors and books.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name a rectangle and say it has two long and two short sides" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Ovals
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will name an oval and say that it is like a stretched circle.
successCriteria: Says an oval has no corners
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name circle, square and triangle and count and join groups.
lessons.starter: Show a picture of an egg and say "An egg is an oval. It is like a stretched circle."
teacherActivities: Show an oval and trace its edge.
Compare an oval with a circle.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show an oval and trace its edge. Children: Children trace the shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "An oval has no corners." Children: Children touch the edge.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare an oval with a circle. Children: Child says which is longer.
Step 4. Teacher: Find ovals in pictures. Children: Child finds an oval.

practical.title: Find ovals
steps: Find an oval in a picture.
practical.safety: Use smooth card shapes and an unbreakable mirror. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Compare an oval and a circle side by side.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw an oval in the sand.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says an oval has no corners
lessons.conclusion: Put the shapes away and say oval.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for ovals such as eggs and mirrors at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name an oval and say that it is like a stretched circle" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sorting five shapes
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort shapes into groups by name.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name circle, square and triangle and count and join groups.
lessons.starter: Show a mixed pile of shapes and say "Let us sort them into groups."
teacherActivities: Sort a few shapes and name each group.
Let each child take a shape from the bag and name it.
Put each shape in the correct hoop.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort a few shapes and name each group. Children: Children say the shape names.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child take a shape from the bag and name it. Children: Child names the shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Put each shape in the correct hoop. Children: Child sorts the shape.
Step 4. Teacher: Count each group. Children: Children count the shapes.

practical.title: Sort the shapes
steps: Put it in the right hoop.
practical.safety: Use smooth shapes with no sharp edges and keep them out of mouths. Supervise sorting.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort the shapes by size as well as kind.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the shapes away and say their names.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort shapes cut from paper at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort shapes into groups by name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape train
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make a train from shapes and describe it.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name circle, square and triangle and count and join groups.
lessons.starter: Show a train made of rectangles with circle wheels and say "Today we make a shape train."
teacherActivities: Show the sample train and name the shapes.
Help children choose shapes for the train.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the sample train and name the shapes. Children: Children name the shapes.
Step 2. Teacher: Help children choose shapes for the train. Children: Child chooses shapes.
Step 3. Teacher: Stick the shapes on paper. Children: Child sticks the shapes.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which shapes did you use?" Children: Child names the shapes.

practical.title: Shape train
practical.safety: Use non-toxic glue sticks and supervise so that no glue goes in mouths. Wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Arrange the shapes together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count the wheels and windows.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Hang the trains and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a shape picture with paper at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a train from shapes and describe it" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 shapes check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names and sorts five shapes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name circle, square and triangle and count and join groups.
lessons.starter: Sing the shape song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: feely bag, sorting and shape train.
At each station ask "What shape is this?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: feely bag, sorting and shape train. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What shape is this?" Children: Child names the shape.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Shape stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use smooth shapes only. Keep glue and small items away from mouths.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use three shapes.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to describe the sides and corners.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names rectangle; names oval; sorts five shapes; describes sides and corners.

questions.question: How many sides has a rectangle?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Names and sorts shapes with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names and sorts five shapes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
